transcript.text: my tumble dryer is giving off a burning smell?? is it safe to keep using it

⚠ Stop using this appliance
A burning smell or smoke can mean an electrical fault or a fire risk. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it (or turn it off at the fuse box), and don't run it again — not even as a test — until it has been checked by a qualified engineer. No, it is not safe to keep using it while there is a burning smell. This could indicate a fire risk from lint buildup on the heater or a mechanical issue like a slipping belt. Please switch the dryer off and unplug it immediately. 1. Is the lint filter (usually in the door opening) full of fluff? Clean it thoroughly.
2. Is there a condenser unit or second filter at the bottom front? If so, remove it and rinse off any fluff under the tap. Once you have done this and let everything dry completely, tell me if the smell persists when you plug it back in (do not run it yet).
ok I've already switched it off at the wall. the lint filter is very full, hasn't been cleaned for a few weeks?? is that what caused it? should I clean it or get someone in?

⚠ Stop using this appliance
A very full lint filter is a classic cause of overheating and that burnt-smell because the air can't escape, trapping heat around the heater element. It is definitely worth cleaning it out. However, because there was already a burning smell, please do not run the dryer yet. A blocked condenser or vent hose (if you have one) could also be causing the same issue. Please clean the lint filter and check/clean any other filters or vents as described above. Let me know if the smell persists once everything is dry.

ok I've cleaned nothing yet, it's still off at the wall. the hose behind it is squashed and has fluff in the end too?? is that a problem? the dryer is in a cupboard with the door shut and a laundry basket on top, does that matter?

⚠ Stop using this appliance
Yes, both the squashed hose with fluff and the cupboard location are major problems. A blocked hose traps hot air inside the dryer, causing it to overheat rapidly, while a closed cupboard stops fresh air from entering, making the overheating even worse. This is exactly why you smell burning lint. Please unplug the machine again (safety first). Straighten or replace that squashed hose and clear all fluff from it. Then move the dryer out of the cupboard so there is plenty of air around it (at least 10cm clearance on all sides). Once you have done this safely with the power off, let me know if the smell has gone away after cleaning the filters. If the smell persists even when unplugged and cool, do not use it and call an engineer.
ok I can clean the filter and pull it out of the cupboard?? but I'm nervous about the hose, I don't want to break something. Is it safe to run it again after that or should I get an engineer anyway?

⚠ Stop using this appliance
To answer your question directly: it is not safe to run the dryer until you have fixed the hose and moved it out of the cupboard. The squashed hose is trapping heat, which causes the burning smell and fire risk. You don't need special tools for this—just unplug it, straighten the hose so air can flow freely, clear any fluff from the end, and pull the dryer forward into open space (not in a closed cupboard). If the smell persists after these changes, or if you see scorch marks inside, then yes, call an engineer.
ok, so if I clean the filter, straighten the hose and move it out of the cupboard it should be fine to run again?? or should I still get someone to look at it since it smelled so strongly?

⚠ Stop using this appliance
You are right to be cautious. The strong smell suggests it did overheat significantly. While cleaning the filter and fixing the hose removes the cause of the overheating, the heat might have already damaged an internal component like the thermal cut-out or the heater element itself. It is safe for you to clean the filter and straighten the hose yourself; these are simple mechanical tasks that won't break anything. However, I would strongly recommend getting a qualified engineer to look at it before running it again, especially if the smell was very strong or if there were any signs of scorching. If you do decide to try it after fixing the airflow, run it empty for just 5 minutes and stay nearby—if you smell burning again, switch it off immediately.
